verification.reason: The head adds a `/** ... */` block above `packages` in `CheckRequestInput`. The pipeline index does not export `CheckRequestInput` or `check-request.ts`. I read all of `index.ts` and found neither. AGENTS.md:33 says "TSDoc only on exported package API. Nothing on internals." A progress-log entry shows the same rule applied to this type before: the `lang` field's TSDoc became a line comment. The base file already carries TSDoc on other fields of this type, such as `install` and `tools`. That is an older breach of the same rule, and it doesn't excuse the new block. The new block is a head-added line that breaks the rule, and P3 fits a documentation-style nit.

I traced the scenario through the walk. The root `node_modules` is scanned in mode "modules". For the entry `@earendil-works`, `#follow(path, "scope")` records a "links" entry and queues `[store, "scope"]` at line 172. Queued work runs only after the synchronous root scan, so the entry `store` is always scanned first, in mode "package" (line 214 to 215), whatever order readdir returns. That scan adds `store` to `#entered`, and its children, including `pi-ai`, get mode "tree", which keys no manifest. When the queued `[store, "scope"]` item is entered, `#scan` returns at line 186 because `store` is already entered. `store/pi-ai/package.json` is therefore never read by `#release`, so `Install.digest` stays the same when pi-ai's version changes. `lensRequest` uses `melianInstall().digest` as `packages` (lens-request.ts:128), and nothing else in this walk keys pi-ai's version. The link stays inside the root, so `outside` is empty and `identified` is true, and reuse is not blocked. The gap is real. It needs a symlinked scope directory that points at a sibling directory already scanned as a package, which is an unusual layout.

checks.ts:718 wires the Melian install digest and identified flag into the check request. No test exercises that wiring. check-request.test.ts supplies its own `packages` object (line 16), and check-requests.test.ts never mentions install or packages. A search of the pipeline tests for `melianInstall` shows no test tying it to the check request. Replacing the line with a constant would pass the suite.
